clue.text: He takes off to do a strip perhaps

definitions.note: to take off someone is to mimic them, so this is a mimic

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words do a strip are only one possible arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: A man removes his clothes, maybe to perform a striptease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes off' suggests undressing, matching 'strip', but it means mimics; 'perhaps' rearranges DO A STRIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A parodist imitates others mockingly, which is what someone who takes them off does.

clue.text: Aching for farmers to get in the vessel

indicators.note: to get in says the farmers go inside the vessel

parts.note: a pail is a bucket, a vessel
the NFU is the National Farmers' Union of Britain

explanation.surface: Farmers struggle to climb into a container, which hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: The NFU is the British farmers' trade body, inserted into PAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something painful is sore, so it makes you ache.

clue.text: Deviously tries to Include Stanley in opposition

indicators.note: to include says the jumbled letters take the short name inside them
deviously means in a roundabout, crooked way, so the letters of tries are twisted

parts.note: Stan is short for Stanley

explanation.surface: Someone cunningly tries to bring Stanley into the opposition party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in opposition' sounds political, matching Stanley's party; it simply means opposing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being resistant means standing against something, opposing it.

clue.text: Swell note one way to finish

parts.note: D is a musical note
one is the Roman numeral I
St is the abbreviation for street, a way
an end is a finish

explanation.surface: A great note: one way to round things off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' looks like the old slang for excellent; it is the verb to bulge.
explanation.definitionFit: To distend is to swell or expand outwards from inner pressure.

clue.text: Ship wrecked by Master East

indicators.note: wrecked means ruined, so the letters of master and the compass point are broken up

explanation.surface: A ship's captain from the east wrecks a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamer is a ship driven by steam power.

clue.text: Short hole in three? Nonsense, a birdie!

parts.note: a short golf hole is usually a par three, so this gives par
rot is nonsense, rubbish talk

explanation.surface: A golfer holes a short par three in two shots and cries out in delight at a birdie.
explanation.walkthrough: The golfing surface makes 'birdie' a score of one under par; here it is just a small bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A parrot is a kind of bird, and birdie is a childish word for any bird.

clue.text: Crowd in Scotland go to recruitment party

parts.note: a press is a crowd or throng
gang is Scots dialect for go

explanation.surface: A crowd in Scotland heads off to a recruiting event.
explanation.walkthrough: Gang is the Scots verb for go, as in Burns's 'gang aft agley'.
explanation.definitionFit: Press gangs were bands that forcibly enlisted men into the navy.

clue.text: He takes the practical view about a material

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a list is a strip of cloth, the selvage edge of woven material

explanation.surface: A man has a pragmatic opinion on some fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: List is an old word for the edge strip of a woven fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist is someone who sees things as they are, not as they might wish.

clue.text: Binds, as the daily help does?

definitions.meaning: to bind is to compel by duty, oblige being to put under obligation
a daily cleaner, or char, is said to oblige her employer, doing for them

explanation.walkthrough: A daily is a British cleaner who comes in each day; she was said to 'oblige' the household she cleaned for.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone under a duty is to bind them, and helping out is doing a favour.

clue.text: Stubborn demand since one anyhow holds the gun

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: holds says the jumbled letters keep the gun inside them
anyhow means in a careless, disordered way, so the letters of since plus one are mixed up

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: Someone keeps insisting on something because they have a gun in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'one' as a person holding a gun; it is the Roman numeral, and the Sten is a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Insistence is a firm, persistent demand that will not be refused.

clue.text: A friend of everyone ere journey's end

indicators.note: ere is an old word for before, putting one piece ahead of the next

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: end picks the final letter of the word journey

explanation.surface: Someone is a companion to all before they finish a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is a supporter or companion on your side.

clue.text: Pope's adornment of Walton's circle

parts.note: Izaak Walton wrote The Compleat Angler, so the fisherman's
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: The Pope wears something that came from the circle of the angler Izaak Walton.
explanation.walkthrough: Izaak Walton was the 17th-century English author of The Compleat Angler, the classic book on fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: The signet worn by each pope bears St Peter casting a net, recalling his trade on the lake.

clue.text: In real trouble, a terrible end for the swimmer

indicators.note: terrible signals that the jumbled letters and the word end are badly mixed up again together
in trouble means in a mess, so the letters of real are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A swimmer in real difficulties meets a dreadful death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' scrambles REAL and 'terrible' mixes that with END. Apt too: in Greek myth Leander drowned swimming the Hellespont to meet Hero.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend this youth swam nightly across the Hellespont to his lover Hero until he drowned.

clue.text: Mundane type pulled from bed by proverbial early riser

definitions.text: Mundane type pulled from bed by proverbial early riser

parts.words: Mundane type pulled from bed by proverbial early riser
parts.note: mundane means of the earth; the proverb says the early bird catches its prey, pulling it from its bed of soil

explanation.definitionFit: This soil creature is earthy by name and, per the proverb, caught by the early bird.

clue.text: A musical boutique ? Imagine that!

parts.note: a free musical composition shares its name with a shop of fancy goods, and with the act of imagining something unreal

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a fanciful free-form piece of music and a flight of imagination.

clue.text: Flattery, and a guilt complex

definitions.note: a noun standing for the verbal noun, the act of fawning praise

indicators.note: complex means intricate and tangled, so these letters are tangled up

explanation.surface: Someone suffers both flattery and a guilt complex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guilt complex' looks like one phrase; 'complex' is the signal to rearrange AND A GUILT.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulation is excessive admiring praise, so heaping it on someone is flattering them.

clue.text: Lace-makers in rags

definitions.meaning: people who tat, making lace by knotting thread with a shuttle
torn shreds of clothing; someone in rags is dressed in torn clothing

explanation.definitionFit: Tatting is a kind of handmade lace, and torn shreds of cloth are a second, unrelated sense.

clue.text: Ice-cream vendor also supplies some giant onions

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An ice-cream seller also sells huge onions.
explanation.walkthrough: Antonio was the stock name for an Italian ice-cream seller in British comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian immigrants ran many British ice-cream businesses, so an Italian forename typified the trader.

clue.text: Article on taboos of ancient Greeks

indicators.note: on places the first word ahead of the next in a down clue

parts.note: the is the definite article
bans are prohibitions, taboos

explanation.surface: A written piece about the prohibitions of the classical Greeks.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a major city of classical Greece; its citizens were its people.

clue.text: Stranded at Lord's ?

definitions.meaning: a ship stranded is stuck on the shore or the bottom
Lord's is a cricket ground, so someone there is at a ground

explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the famous London cricket ground, so split the word as 'a ground'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship run onto the shore is stuck, and Lord's is a sporting arena: split the word in two.

clue.text: Road ran tortuously in the Pyrenees

indicators.note: tortuously means twisting and winding, so the letters are twisted round

explanation.surface: A road winds its way through the Pyrenean mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a small principality set high in the mountains between France and Spain.

clue.text: Cancel order for cinders

indicators.note: order for means put the letters of cinders into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone revokes an order for ashes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a purchase request; it means arrange the letters of CINDERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescind a law or contract is to revoke or annul it.

clue.text: Doctor Sharp fished for oysters

parts.note: edged means sharp, having a cutting edge

explanation.surface: A doctor called Sharp went oyster fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharp' reads as the doctor's surname; it is a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Oysters are gathered by dragging a dredge net along the seabed.

clue.text: Commons being property neither real nor personal, but this

definitions.meaning: the common people, the class below nobility and clergy

definitions.text: being property neither real nor personal, but this
definitions.meaning: estate is property, divided into real and personal kinds; a further sort would be a third kind

explanation.walkthrough: In law estate (property) is either real (land) or personal (goods); the joke invents a third kind.
explanation.definitionFit: In pre-revolutionary France the commoners formed the class after clergy and nobles in the Estates-General.

clue.text: She gets an article reversed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: reversed says the article is written backwards after the first piece

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A woman receives a piece of writing sent back to her.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna is a woman's name, so it can stand for any she.

clue.text: Ignoring objection concerning old county, division

parts.note: over can mean about or concerning, as in a row over money
Yorkshire was divided into three ridings until 1974

explanation.surface: A dispute about a former county boundary goes ahead despite protests.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire, a large English county, was split into North, East and West Ridings until 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: Overriding a veto means setting aside the protest and proceeding anyway.

clue.text: One's apparently late playing this

parts.note: late here means dead: an animal famed for feigning death when threatened gives an idiom for pretending

explanation.definitionFit: To play this American marsupial is an idiom for pretending to be dead or asleep.

clue.text: Strip the elderly, like mummy?

parts.note: a band is a strip of material
the aged are the elderly

explanation.surface: Someone undresses an old person, rather like a mother might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mummy' looks like a mother; it is an Egyptian mummy, wrapped in strips of linen.
explanation.definitionFit: An Egyptian mummy is swathed head to toe in linen wrappings.
